key_insight: The paper shows that neutral-atom compilation can be accelerated by turning hardware constraints into algebraic decomposition problems for single-qubit gates and graph-scheduling problems for C-Z gates.
engineering_relevance: This provides a practical way to cut addressing layers and atom transport overhead in scalable neutral-atom quantum processors, improving circuit execution efficiency.
method: Exploit matrix-level structure of single-qubit gate families to find efficient rank-one decompositions.
Model C-Z transport scheduling with graph-theoretic formulations and coloring-based algorithms.
Use provable compilation strategies tailored to realistic 2D neutral-atom hardware constraints.
evidence_signal: In numerical experiments, the methods reduce addressing layers by up to 2×, cut C-Z transport operations by about 50%, and lower MaxCut QAOA transport cost by more than 30% on average.
watch_item: The gains depend on structured gate families and realistic transport models, so performance may vary for less regular circuits or hardware with different control constraints.
paper_title: Structure-Aware Compilation for Scalable Neutral-Atom Quantum Computing
